evidence.note: Early recon identified block types and analyzed raw-block files (simple.zst), producing implicit sub-goals and a conceptual sense of the format hierarchy before coding.

Stated a nominal milestone/dependency plan: build 'raw blocks and compressed blocks with predefined modes at minimum, then extend', compiling 'after each part' — a sensible ordering in the agent's head.

Raw blocks genuinely landed and verified (2/6 tests pass); this is the one real 'this feature works' checkpoint. Compressed blocks (4 fails) were treated as a single undifferentiated bundle rather than per-subsystem milestones.

The entire decoder was repeatedly deleted and rewritten from scratch (~15 times) as one monolithic file; FSE, Huffman, and sequences stayed entangled and were never isolated or independently tested — the stated incremental plan was not sustained.

Long circular debugging of FSE/reverse-bit-reader/predefined-tables all at once; no smallest-possible per-subsystem test input, milestones degenerated into 'rewrite the complete decoder', ending still failing on all compressed blocks.

reasoning: The agent showed a sensible conceptual dependency ordering (raw → compressed → FSE → Huffman → sequences) and did land and checkpoint raw blocks as a working feature, which lifts it above a pure 3. But the harder compressed subsystems were built as one entangled monolithic push and wholesale-rewritten ~15 times, none testable in isolation, with milestones effectively reduced to 'write/rewrite the complete decoder' — squarely matching the anchor-3 description for most of the horizon. The stated incremental intent was never sustained, so the observed level sits between anchors 3 and 5, at 4.
